sourceType: Official Government of Punjab tourism website
note: Facts extracted below; prose summaries are written in our own words, not copied verbatim from the source.
about: Border district on the Sutlej River, founded either by Firoz Shah Tughlaq or a Bhatti chief Feroze Khan. Site of the Anglo-Sikh Wars (1845-49), Bhagat Singh/Rajguru/Sukhdev's cremation at Hussainiwala (1931), and the 1897 Battle of Saragarhi memory.

places.name: National Martyrs Memorial, Hussainiwala
places.facts: Built 1968; honors Bhagat Singh, Rajguru and Sukhdev, secretly cremated here 23 March 1931 after execution at Lahore Central Jail. Life-sized black granite statues of the three martyrs. B.K. Dutt also cremated here per his wish. Annual Shaheedi Mela on 23 March. Preserved section of the old Ferozepur-Lahore railway line.

places.name: Indo-Pakistan Retreat Ceremony, Hussainiwala Border
places.facts: 40-minute joint BSF/Pakistan Rangers flag de-hoisting ceremony, mirroring Attari-Wagah.

places.name: Shan-e-Hind Gate, Hussainiwala
places.timings: Visible at all hours; evening ceremony daily
places.facts: 42ft long x 91ft wide x 56ft high gate, built as a counterpart to Pakistan's 30ft Fakhr-e-Pak structure.

places.name: Anglo-Sikh War Memorial, Ferozeshah
places.location: Ferozeshah, ~16 km from Ferozepur on Moga Road
places.facts: Honors soldiers of the Anglo-Sikh Wars (Mudki, Ferozeshah, Sabhraon, Chellianwala, 1845-49); 3-storey building designed by H.S. Chopra; displays period weapons from the Patiala Museum and 4 large battle paintings by Kirpal Singh.

places.name: Saragarhi Memorial Gurdwara, Ferozepur Cantonment
places.location: Ferozepur Cantonment, 2 km from Ferozepur Cantonment Railway Station
places.facts: Honors 21 Sikh soldiers of the 36th Sikh Regiment (raised at Ferozepur in 1887) who died defending Fort Saragarhi on 12 September 1897 against ~10,000 Pathans. Built 1904 at cost of Rs 27,118, opened by Sir Charles Rivaz.

places.name: Barki Memorial, Ferozepur Cantonment
places.location: Ferozepur Cantonment, part of Saragarhi Complex
places.facts: Built 1969 for soldiers of the 7 Infantry Division who died in the 1965 war fall of Barki. 27-foot red/white sandstone pillar, a Patton tank and Barki milestone nearby.

places.name: Harike Wildlife Sanctuary
places.timings: Daylight hours; early morning best for birdwatching
places.facts: 86 sq km, declared Wildlife Sanctuary 1999, Ramsar Site since 1990; ~375 bird species recorded, up to 45,000 ducks in peak season.

places.name: Chak Sarkar Forest, Mamdot
places.facts: Reserved Forest along the India-Pakistan boundary.

places.name: Gurdwara Shri Jaamani Sahib, Bazidpur
places.location: Village Bazidpur, 8 km from Ferozepur on Ferozepur-Ludhiana Road
places.facts: Associated with Guru Gobind Singh Ji after the Battle of Muktsar; also known as Gurdwara Gurusar or Tittarsar.

howToReach.air: Sri Guru Ram Dass Ji International Airport, Amritsar (~124km)
howToReach.rail: Ferozepur Cantonment and Ferozepur City railway stations, Northern Railway junction
howToReach.road: Bus Stand Ferozepur City and Cantonment Bus Stand
